body:
Summary

I am seeing a regression with two Intel Arc Pro B60 GPUs on Fedora 43.

With the Fedora 43 Intel GPU runtime stack at 26.09.37435.12-4.fc43, each GPU works individually when selected with ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=0 or ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=1, but exposing both GPUs together with ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=0,1 causes PyTorch XPU device enumeration to fail inside:

torch._C._xpu_getDeviceCount()

The failure is:

RuntimeError: level_zero backend failed with error: 2147483646 (UR_RESULT_ERROR_UNKNOWN)

Downgrading the Intel GPU runtime stack to 25.31.34666.3-1.fc43 fixes dual-device enumeration: torch._C._xpu_getDeviceCount() returns 2.

Hardware

Two Intel Arc Pro B60 GPUs.

Both appear in sysfs:

/sys/class/drm/renderD128/device
vendor: 0x8086
device: 0xe211
driver: /sys/bus/pci/drivers/xe

/sys/class/drm/renderD129/device
vendor: 0x8086
device: 0xe211
driver: /sys/bus/pci/drivers/xe

OS / environment

Fedora 43 container on Fedora host, using Intel Arc Pro B60 GPUs passed through.

Kernel driver:

xe

Python environment:

Python: 3.12
torch: 2.11.0+xpu

Also reproduced with:

torch: 2.13.0.dev20260503+xpu

Broken package versions

Dual-GPU enumeration fails with:

intel-compute-runtime-26.09.37435.12-4.fc43.x86_64
intel-level-zero-26.09.37435.12-4.fc43.x86_64
intel-level-zero-devel-26.09.37435.12-4.fc43.x86_64
intel-opencl-26.09.37435.12-4.fc43.x86_64
intel-ocloc-26.09.37435.12-4.fc43.x86_64
intel-gmmlib-22.9.0-1.fc43.x86_64
intel-igc-2.30.3-1.fc43.x86_64
intel-igc-libs-2.30.3-1.fc43.x86_64

Working package versions

Dual-GPU enumeration works after downgrading to:

intel-compute-runtime-25.31.34666.3-1.fc43.x86_64
intel-level-zero-25.31.34666.3-1.fc43.x86_64
intel-level-zero-devel-25.31.34666.3-1.fc43.x86_64
intel-opencl-25.31.34666.3-1.fc43.x86_64
intel-ocloc-25.31.34666.3-1.fc43.x86_64
intel-gmmlib-22.8.2-1.fc43.x86_64
intel-igc-2.16.0-1.fc43.x86_64
intel-igc-libs-2.16.0-1.fc43.x86_64

Reproducer

Single GPU 0 works:

source /opt/vllm-xpu/bin/activate

unset SYCL_DEVICE_FILTER
unset ZE_ENABLE_ALT_DRIVERS
unset ZE_FLAT_DEVICE_HIERARCHY

export ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=level_zero:gpu
export ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=0

python - <<'PY'
import torch, os
print("ZE_AFFINITY_MASK:", os.environ.get("ZE_AFFINITY_MASK"))
print("torch:", torch.version)
print("xpu available:", torch.xpu.is_available())
print("xpu count:", torch.xpu.device_count())
for i in range(torch.xpu.device_count()):
torch.xpu.set_device(i)
print(i, torch.xpu.get_device_name(i))
PY

Output:

ZE_AFFINITY_MASK: 0
torch: 2.11.0+xpu
xpu available: True
xpu count: 1
0 Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics

Single GPU 1 works:

export ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=1

python - <<'PY'
import torch, os
print("ZE_AFFINITY_MASK:", os.environ.get("ZE_AFFINITY_MASK"))
print("torch:", torch.version)
print("xpu available:", torch.xpu.is_available())
print("xpu count:", torch.xpu.device_count())
for i in range(torch.xpu.device_count()):
torch.xpu.set_device(i)
print(i, torch.xpu.get_device_name(i))
PY

Output:

ZE_AFFINITY_MASK: 1
torch: 2.11.0+xpu
xpu available: True
xpu count: 1
0 Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics

Both GPUs fail on 26.09:

export ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=0,1

python - <<'PY'
import torch, os, traceback
print("ZE_AFFINITY_MASK:", os.environ.get("ZE_AFFINITY_MASK"))
print("torch:", torch.version)
print("calling torch._C._xpu_getDeviceCount()")
try:
print("count:", torch._C._xpu_getDeviceCount())
except Exception:
traceback.print_exc()
PY

Output on 26.09.37435.12:

ZE_AFFINITY_MASK: 0,1
torch: 2.11.0+xpu
calling torch._C._xpu_getDeviceCount()
RuntimeError: level_zero backend failed with error: 2147483646 (UR_RESULT_ERROR_UNKNOWN)

Both GPUs work on 25.31:

After downgrading to the 25.31.34666.3 package set:

export ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=0,1
export ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR=level_zero:gpu

python - <<'PY'
import torch
print("torch:", torch.version)
print("count:", torch._C._xpu_getDeviceCount())
for i in range(torch.xpu.device_count()):
print(i, torch.xpu.get_device_name(i))
PY

Output:

torch: 2.11.0+xpu
count: 2
0 Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics
1 Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics

Native Level Zero device enumeration

A small C Level Zero test using zeInit, zeDriverGet, zeDeviceGet, and zeDeviceGetProperties can see both devices successfully even when ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=0,1:

zeInit: ZE_RESULT_SUCCESS
zeDriverGet count: 1
Driver 0 zeDeviceGet count: 2

Device 0:
name: Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics
deviceId: 0xe211
uuid includes PCI/device marker ... 0c ...

Device 1:
name: Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics
deviceId: 0xe211
uuid includes PCI/device marker ... 45 ...

So basic Level Zero enumeration appears to work, but the PyTorch/SYCL/UR path fails when creating or initializing the two-device context on 26.09.

Notes

The failure is not that either card is bad. Each card works individually.

This appears to be a regression between:

25.31.34666.3 -> works with two B60s
26.09.37435.12 -> fails with two B60s

Please let me know if this should instead be filed against the Unified Runtime / Intel LLVM SYCL stack. I am filing here first because the behavior tracks the intel-compute-runtime / intel-level-zero package version.
Can confirm, the regression is between NEO 25.40 and 25.48.

25.44 changed BMG internal engine/context initialization from eager to deferred.
This may have caused Level Zero device creation/enumeration to fail in multi-BMG systems because an internal BCS context was not initialized early enough.

I think the multi-GPU enumeration regression may be related to the BMG internal engine/context initialization changes between 25.40.35563.4 and 25.44.36015.5.

Working version:
- intel-compute-runtime / intel-level-zero 25.40.35563.4

Broken version:
- intel-compute-runtime / intel-level-zero 25.44.36015.5 / 25.44.36015.8

Observed behaviour:
- System has two Intel BMG discrete GPUs.
- Older runtime enumerates both GPUs correctly.
- Newer 25.44 runtime does not enumerate both GPUs correctly.
- This appears before vLLM/oneCCL involvement, so it looks like a Level Zero / compute-runtime device discovery or device initialization issue.

Suspicious change:
Commit cf3f5d74994a2aaa9dc728f4a8b8c32ab7bec78b

Title:
performance: defer internal context init, ptl, bmg

This added/changed BMG/PTL product-helper behaviour so that internal engine initialization is deferred:

    bool ProductHelperHw<gfxProduct>::initializeInternalEngineImmediately() const {
        return false;
    }

For BMG this is in:

    shared/source/xe2_hpg_core/bmg/os_agnostic_product_helper_bmg.inl

For PTL this is in:

    shared/source/xe3_core/ptl/os_agnostic_product_helper_ptl.inl

The likely behavioural change is:

Before:
- Internal engines/contexts were initialized immediately during device setup unless otherwise overridden.

After:
- BMG/PTL explicitly defer internal engine/context initialization.

There is also a follow-up commit that looks directly related:

Commit a673c5deeab3c907f0c253e37ac08dffb614b92d

Title:
fix: always initialize internal bcs engine

This changed OsContext::isImmediateContextInitializationEnabled() from effectively:

    if (engineUsage == EngineUsage::internal) {
        return initializeInternalEngineImmediately;
    }

to:

    if (engineUsage == EngineUsage::internal) {
        return initializeInternalEngineImmediately || engineType == aub_stream::EngineType::ENGINE_BCS;
    }

File:

    shared/source/os_interface/os_context.cpp

That follow-up suggests the original deferred-initialization change may have deferred too much, and that internal BCS still needs to be initialized eagerly.

My theory:
- The 25.44 runtime changed BMG internal engine/context initialization from eager to deferred.
- In a multi-BMG system, the Level Zero device creation/enumeration path may still rely on an internal BCS/context being available during early device setup.
- As a result, the second GPU may fail initialization or be skipped during enumeration.
- The later “always initialize internal bcs engine” fix looks like it may be addressing exactly this class of fallout.

Suggested thing to check:
- Does 25.44.36015.5 / 25.44.36015.8 include the BMG deferred internal context init change without the correct internal BCS eager-init behaviour?
- If so, can the BCS eager-init fix be backported to the affected 25.44 package?
- Alternatively, can BMG temporarily revert initializeInternalEngineImmediately() to true to confirm whether enumeration recovers?

Minimal test patch idea:

    if (engineUsage == EngineUsage::internal) {
        return initializeInternalEngineImmediately || engineType == aub_stream::EngineType::ENGINE_BCS;
    }

in:

    shared/source/os_interface/os_context.cpp

If that restores enumeration of both BMG GPUs, it would strongly indicate the regression is caused by the deferred internal context/engine initialization change rather than PCIe topology, vLLM, or oneCCL.

After forcing BMG initializeInternalEngineImmediately() back to true and rebuilding compute-runtime 26.09.37435.12, both B60 GPUs enumerate and zeDeviceCanAccessPeer() reports peer access in both directions:

Drivers: 1
Driver 0 devices: 2
Device 0: Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics device=0xe211
Device 1: Intel(R) Arc(TM) Pro B60 Graphics device=0xe211
P2P 0 -> 1: ze_result=0x0 canAccess=1
P2P 1 -> 0: ze_result=0x0 canAccess=1

The only source change was:

shared/source/xe2_hpg_core/bmg/os_agnostic_product_helper_bmg.inl

ProductHelperHw<gfxProduct>::initializeInternalEngineImmediately()

from:
    return false;

to:
    return true;

This confirms the regression is tied to the BMG deferred internal engine/context initialization path, and not to PCIe topology or Level Zero P2P capability on this system.

4× Intel Arc Pro B70 (BMG-G31, 0xe223), Arch Linux + oneAPI 2025.3. Tried ~14 build combinations of compute-runtime 26.05 / 26.09 / 26.14 / 26.18, with the BMG initializeInternalEngineImmediately() one-line patch, with and without intel-graphics-compiler 2.35.2 built from source (clang+libc++) and intel-gmmlib's igfxfmid.h patched to define IGFX_NVL. Every 26.x driver either fails to compile, crashes at `sycl-ls`, or aborts at runtime in `shared/source/gmm_helper/client_context/gmm_client_context.cpp:50` (ABI mismatch between compute-runtime built against the patched IGFX enum and the installed libgmm.so built without it). The BMG one-liner is necessary but not sufficient — david-bue's SVMAllocsManager::createUnifiedMemoryAllocatiofinding on #916 matches our observations exactly. 25.40.35563.4-4 remains the only working pin on this hardware. Endorsing bisect of dc85f33e49 ("fix: Disallow USM compression on peer access", NEO-15427) as the prime suspect.

<details>
  <summary>Click to expand</summary>
  
# compute-runtime#921 — full diagnosis after on-rig instrumentation

Hardware: 4× Intel Arc Pro B70 (BMG, xe2_hpg_core, device 0xe223), xe kernel driver, Manjaro 7.0.3.

## Bug, restated precisely

When multiple BMG devices are exposed to a single process, `sycl::context(vector<device>)` throws `UR_RESULT_ERROR_UNKNOWN`. Same for any tool that triggers multi-device UR context construction (`llama-ls-sycl-device`, `llama-cli --list-devices` with both cards, vLLM with `tensor_parallel_size>1`, etc.).

## The actual root cause

The xe kernel driver rejects `DRM_IOCTL_XE_VM_BIND` with **`EINVAL` (22)** when binding a peer-imported (DMA-buf imported from another BMG device) buffer object to the peer device's VM. This happens **on every engine on the peer device** — CCS, BCS, all of them. The bind fails regardless of engine type or `vmBindFlags`.

Captured from the rig with printf instrumentation in compute-runtime:

```
bind BO-33 to VM 1, vmHandleId = 0,
range: ffffc001ffc20000 - ffffc001ffc30000, size: 65536,
result: -1, errno: 22 (Invalid argument)
```

This means: when compute-runtime's peer-import (`getPeerAllocation` → `importFdHandle` → `createGraphicsAllocationFromSharedHandle`) gives the kernel a DMA-buf FD from device 0 and asks the kernel to bind it into device 1's VM at the same GPU VA as the source, the kernel says no. compute-runtime has done its part correctly — the FD is valid, the GEM handle on the peer device is valid, the VA range is valid (size, alignment, no overlap). The kernel just won't bind it.

This is a kernel-side limitation of the xe driver shipped with Manjaro 7.0.3. It's outside compute-runtime's reach to fully fix.

## How the symptom escalates to `UR_RESULT_ERROR_UNKNOWN`

1. SYCL `sycl::context(vector<device>)` → UR `urContextCreate`. The V2 UR adapter (default for BMG IP version 20.2.0) decides to allocate a 1-byte device USM on device 0 and then call `zeContextMakeMemoryResident(device_1, ptr, size)` to mirror it onto every peer device in the context — that's its "validate the multi-device context is usable" handshake.
2. compute-runtime `Context::makeMemoryResident(device_1, ptr, size)`:
   - `getDriverSystemMemoryAllocation(ptr, size, root=1)` returns `nullptr` (alloc isn't tracked on device 1)
   - falls through to `findAllocationDataForRange` + `getPeerAllocation(device_1, allocData, ptr, ...)`
   - `getPeerAllocation` peer-imports the source FD to device 1 via `peekInternalHandle` → `importFdHandle(neoDevice_1, basePointer=src_VA)` — succeeds, returns the peer-mapped GraphicsAllocation
   - then `memoryOperationsIface->makeResident(neoDevice_1, peerAlloc, true, true)` iterates `device_1->getAllEngines()` and calls `bo->bind` for each
3. The very first `bo->bind` (or any subsequent one) hits the EINVAL from xe and `DrmMemoryOperationsHandlerBind::makeResidentWithinOsContext` returns `MemoryOperationsStatus::outOfMemory`
4. `Context::makeMemoryResident` maps that to `ZE_RESULT_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY (0x70000003)`
5. The V2 UR adapter propagates as `UR_RESULT_ERROR_UNKNOWN (2147483646)` from `urContextCreate`
6. SYCL throws.

The V1 adapter doesn't take this path during context construction — it ignores residency failures and trusts that residency will be established lazily. That's why "V1 enumerates fine" was a misleading data point in the #921 thread: V1 doesn't actually run cross-device anything either; it just doesn't fail at construction time. Once you `malloc_device` and try to use it cross-device on V1, it also throws — confirmed on the rig.

## Why prior hypotheses didn't hold up

| Hypothesis | What rig instrumentation showed |
|---|---|
| Deferred internal engine init on BMG (`cf3f5d7499`) — fix by setting `initializeInternalEngineImmediately() = true` | Necessary but unrelated to the multi-device bug. Without the patch, even single-device init has issues; with the patch, single-device works. The multi-device bug is downstream of this. ClancyBuf's 2×B60 success is a stronger reproducer than B70 because B60 may have different kernel-side acceptance — but on 4×B70 the patch alone is insufficient. |
| `dc85f33e49` USM-compression-on-peer-access regression — fix by reverting | Reverting actually makes things worse (forces compressed=1 on the peer-probe allocation). On the production `compute-runtime-26.05.37020.3 + BMG one-liner + dc85f33e49 revert` build, instrumentation shows `compressed=1` going into the peer bind. Restoring `dc85f33e49` makes the alloc go in with `compressed=0` (correct), but the kernel still rejects the bind. The revert in `~/build/compute-runtime-pkg/020-revert-dc85f33e49-usm-compression-peer-access.patch` should be dropped. |
| Bind eventually succeeds later in the trace — fix by retry | The "later success" is a different GEM handle that happens to reuse the same BO number. With the permissive variant (continue past failures, no early break in `DrmMemoryOperationsHandlerBind::makeResident`), all 5 engines on the peer device fail with EINVAL — not engine-specific. |
| Internal-RCS context still deferred | Wrong premise. BMG's default engine type is CCS, not RCS. The internal-default-engine context that stays deferred on BMG is internal-CCS, which `initializeResources(false, ...)` explicitly initializes inside `DrmMemoryOperationsHandlerBind::makeResident` before each bind attempt. Engine init isn't the missing prerequisite. |

## What a fix CAN do at the compute-runtime layer

Given that the kernel-side bind is unfixable from userspace, compute-runtime has two realistic options:

### Option A — skip eager makeResident for peer-imported allocs

The minimal source change. In `Context::makeMemoryResident`, when `getPeerAllocation` returns a peer-imported `GraphicsAllocation`, return `ZE_RESULT_SUCCESS` without calling `memoryOperationsIface->makeResident`. The DMA-buf import has already mapped the BO into the peer device's address space at the source VA, which is what residency means at the user level. Lazy bind happens later when a command list actually submits work that needs the BO resident.

**Validated on the rig (build #N+1, with this patch only, no others):**
- 2-device `sycl::context()` → **OK**
- 4-device `sycl::context()` → **OK**
- 2-device + 4-device `sycl::context()` are reproducible PASS

**Does NOT fix:**
- Cross-device `q1.memcpy(b_on_dev1, a_on_dev0)` — the BCS submission path also calls `makeResident` for the peer allocation and that also hits the same xe EINVAL. So actual cross-device kernel workloads still fail.

This is still a worthwhile PR because:
- It fixes the `UR_RESULT_ERROR_UNKNOWN` thrown from `sycl::context()` itself, which is what breaks `sycl-ls`, `llama-cli --list-devices`, vLLM device discovery, and any other tool that tries to enumerate multiple BMG cards. These tools don't actually use cross-device memory — they just need the context to construct.
- It makes V2-adapter behavior match V1-adapter behavior at this exact decision point: V1 also ignores the failure here.
- It's the smallest possible change, easy to review and revert.

The diff:

```diff
diff --git a/level_zero/core/source/context/context.cpp b/level_zero/core/source/context/context.cpp
@@ -686,12 +686,21 @@ ze_result_t Context::makeMemoryResident(ze_device_handle_t hDevice, void *ptr, s
     auto allocation = device->getDriverHandle()->getDriverSystemMemoryAllocation(
         ptr,
         size,
         neoDevice->getRootDeviceIndex(),
         nullptr);
+    bool isPeerImportedAllocation = false;
     if (allocation == nullptr) {
         NEO::SvmAllocationData *allocData = nullptr;
         bool foundBuffer = this->driverHandle->findAllocationDataForRange(ptr, size, allocData);
         if (foundBuffer) {
             uintptr_t alignedPtr = reinterpret_cast<uintptr_t>(ptr);
             allocation = this->driverHandle->getPeerAllocation(device, allocData, ptr, &alignedPtr, nullptr, false);
+            isPeerImportedAllocation = (allocation != nullptr);
         }
         if (allocation == nullptr) {
             return ZE_RESULT_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
         }
     }
+    // Peer-imported allocations have their address-space mapping established by
+    // getPeerAllocation's DMA-buf import. An additional eager per-engine bind via
+    // memoryOperationsIface->makeResident can be rejected by some kernel drivers
+    // (xe / BMG: EINVAL on vmBind of peer-imported BOs) and breaks UR V2 adapter's
+    // multi-device context construction handshake. The actual residency is
+    // established lazily when the peer alloc is used in a command-list submission.
+    if (isPeerImportedAllocation) {
+        return ZE_RESULT_SUCCESS;
+    }
     if (allocation->isLockedMemory()) {
         return ZE_RESULT_ERROR_INVALID_ARGUMENT;
     }
```

The patch in master applies the same way; line numbers shift slightly but the surrounding code is identical.

### Option B — fix the V2 UR adapter to not call `zeContextMakeMemoryResident` on peer devices during multi-device context construction

This is the right architectural fix but lives in `oneapi-src/unified-runtime`, not compute-runtime. A PR there could detect that the destination device is a non-source device in the context and skip the residency mirror. compute-runtime can't influence this from its side.

## Recommendation

Submit Option A upstream as **`fix: skip eager peer-import makeResident in Context::makeMemoryResident`** with the body above. Cite #921, #916, ggml-org/llama.cpp#21747, and note that this fixes the multi-device-enumeration failure for any BMG-using tool. Real cross-device workloads still need either kernel-side xe driver progress on peer-imported BO bind, or for end users to fall back to OpenCL (`ONEAPI_DEVICE_SELECTOR='opencl:gpu'`) which doesn't go through this code path.

For the local rig: drop the `020-revert-dc85f33e49-usm-compression-peer-access.patch` from `~/build/compute-runtime-pkg/PKGBUILD` (it's net-harmful) and add Option A's patch instead. Keep the BMG one-liner (`initializeInternalEngineImmediately()=true`) — it's still required to make single-device init reliable.

## Open questions

1. Is the xe `vmBind EINVAL` on peer-imported BO a known kernel limitation tracked anywhere? — worth posting on intel-xe@lists.freedesktop.org with the trace.
2. Does upstream xe-next have the fix? — worth checking `git log --oneline` in `drivers/gpu/drm/xe/` for "p2p" / "external" / "dma-buf" since 6.18 baseline.
3. Does ARC A770 (also affected per #916) show the same exact failure mode? It's i915 driver, not xe — likely a different root cause, even if the user-visible symptom looks the same.

  
</details>

Arc Pro B60 x2: zeDeviceCanAccessPeer returns YES but peer zeCommandListAppendMemoryCopy fails with ZE_RESULT_ERROR_OUT_OF_DEVICE_MEMORY

Hardware:
- 2x Intel Arc Pro B60, device ID 8086:e211
- AMD AM5 / PCIe 5.0 motherboard
- Both GPUs linked at PCIe 5.0 x8

OS / stack:
- Fedora 44
- Kernel: 7.0.8-200.fc44.x86_64
- Driver: xe

## Multi-device USM device alloc on BMG: peer-read returns garbage from compression-on-peer race

`SVMAllocsManager::createUnifiedMemoryAllocation` disables compression for peer-imported USM allocations via a guard introduced in dc85f33e49 and refactored in 26.18. The guard tests `device->hasAnyPeerAccess().value_or(false)`.

That `std::optional<bool>` is populated lazily by `initializePeerAccessForDevices` at driver init. For the **first** USM device allocation in a multi-device L0 context the value is observed as `Some(false)` — the disable arm is skipped, the BO is allocated compressed, and any later peer-import returns the compressed bytes through dma-buf without surface metadata.

### Repro (BMG, 2× Arc Pro B70, Linux 7.1-rc4 + xe, intel-compute-runtime 26.18.38308.1)

`multi_kernel_test.cpp` (single sycl::malloc_device on dev0 + q_dev1.memcpy):

```
$ ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=0,1 ./multi_kernel_test
[A] single-device           PASS
[B] multi-dev ctx, same dev PASS
[C] dev0 writer / dev1 read FAIL — host[0..3] = 0,0,0,0

$ NEOReadDebugKeys=1 RenderCompressedBuffersEnabled=0 ZE_AFFINITY_MASK=0,1 ./multi_kernel_test
[C] dev0 writer / dev1 read PASS — host[0..3] = 100,101,102,103
```

OpenCL backend aborts at `enqueue_svm.h:308` `UNRECOVERABLE_IF(!allocation)` for the same case.

### Evidence

`fprintf` at the top of `createUnifiedMemoryAllocation` (added for diagnosis):

```
[USM-DBG] createUnif rdi=0 comp_pre=1 nRDIs=2 peerHas=1 peer=0  <-- first alloc: Some(false)
[USM-DBG] createUnif rdi=0 comp_pre=1 nRDIs=2 peerHas=1 peer=1  <-- subsequent allocs
```

Kernel side is correct — bpftrace confirms `xe_dma_buf_map` returns sg_tables with peer-BAR addresses and `xe_pt_insert_entry` commits PTEs at those addresses. The peer reads the *right physical location*; the bytes there are compressed.

### Patch

Single-line conditional addition. Gate also on `memoryProperties.rootDeviceIndices.size() > 1` — that's known synchronously at allocation time and conservatively disables compression for any multi-device context BO (which can become peer-imported later regardless of the current cache state).

```diff
+    const bool multiDeviceContext = (memoryProperties.rootDeviceIndices.size() > 1);
     if (compressionEnabled && memoryProperties.device) {
         auto *releaseHelper = memoryProperties.device->getReleaseHelper();
         if (releaseHelper && !releaseHelper->isUsmCompressionSupportedOnPeerAccess() &&
-            memoryProperties.device->hasAnyPeerAccess().value_or(false)) {
+            (memoryProperties.device->hasAnyPeerAccess().value_or(false) || multiDeviceContext)) {
             compressionEnabled = false;
         }
     }
```

(For 26.18: same `|| multiDeviceContext` addition to the `preferCompressed = false` gate at `unified_memory_manager.cpp:521-525`.)

Verified by rebuilding 26.05 with the patch, loading via `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`: repro case C passes 5/5 runs. Reverting the patch on the same build: returns to FAIL.

### Related

- vllm-project/vllm#41663 (same hardware, downstream symptom on TP=2)
- #916, #922 — adjacent multi-device BMG/A770 issues
- Kernel-side prerequisite (xe_dma_buf_pin -EINVAL) fixed by Leon Romanovsky's "dma-buf: Always build with DMABUF_MOVE_NOTIFY" — in mainline 7.1

```
1. kernel ≥ Linux 7.1 (Manjaro linux71 — Leon's MOVE_NOTIFY merged in mainline 7.1)
2. intel-compute-runtime ≥ 26.18 (from extra repo, with pin removed)
3. oneAPI 2026.0+, rebuild your SYCL apps against the new libsycl.so.9 if needed
4. disable VRAM compression for multi-device SYCL workloads:
```

Hi @F3zz1k, @ClancyBuf, @Stoney49th, @arthw, 

Thank you all for reporting this.

There are two distinct issues described here.

1. UR_RESULT_ERROR_UNKNOWN - This is the same issue as in #916. It is already fixed in kernel 7.1+, and for pre-7.1 kernels it is addressed in e91243a9d03de849f45d8b862a62afd4424cff8b.

2. Compression-related issue (the one that the `RenderCompressedBuffersEnabled=0` flag helps with) - This is a regression introduced in e4e871c1af3fb125424f0b067488d238e0f599fd. It should be resolved by 258518f8039afba59c46d98bb7f6f068d12f026d. It also requires kernel 7.1+.

Please let us know whether these updates resolve all of your problems, or if anything still remains.

Thanks again for the report and the great collaboration!
